capitals.name: Vlorë
capitals.note: Seat of the Assembly of Vlorë (28 November 1912) and the Provisional Government (4 December 1912 to 22 January 1914); 'Vlora was the only town in the whole country under the delegates' control'. The pages call Vlorë the assembly's town, not 'capital'.

capitals.name: Durrës
capitals.note: Principality infobox 'Durrës (1914-20)'; Prince Wilhelm arrived 'at his provisional capital of Durrës' on 7 March 1914.

capitals.name: Lushnjë
capitals.note: Infobox 'Lushnjë (1920)'; the Congress of Lushnjë (27-31 January 1920) 'moved the capital from Lushnjë to Tirana'.

capitals.name: Tirana
capitals.note: Infobox 'Tirana (1920-24)'; the Albania page infobox: 'Capital and largest city: Tirana'.

rulers.name: Wilhelm of Wied (Wilhelm I)
rulers.title: Prince
rulers.note: Arrived at Durrës 7 March 1914, 'left Albania on September 3, 1914'; the infobox lists '1914-1925: Wilhelm I', a nominal span. No ruler is named for 1915-1924 on the pages opened.

rulers.name: Ahmet Zogu (Zog I)
rulers.title: President from 1925, King from 1 September 1928
rulers.note: Zogu's army retook Tirana in December 1924 (Principality page); the republic of 31 January 1925 became the Kingdom on 1 September 1928 (Albania page: 'In 1928, Zog transitioned Albania from a republic to a monarchy'); 'On 9 April 1939, Zog I fled to Greece' (World War II page). His presidency is implied, not stated, by the pages.

rulers.name: Victor Emmanuel III of Italy
rulers.title: King, in personal union with Italy
rulers.note: The Albanian parliament voted on 12 April 1939 to unite the country with Italy and offered him the crown; the personal union ended with Italy's capitulation in September 1943.

correction.text: Vlorë, where the Assembly of 40 delegates declared independence on 28 November 1912: 'Vlora was the only town in the whole country under the delegates' control'; held until the Great Powers fixed the borders in July 1913

keyframe_review.note: 17,682 km2 (central and southern Albania south of 41.4 N, all inside the 1913 shape) is the extent the assembly claimed, not what it controlled: the page says Albania 'was occupied by the Balkan League member states' (Serbia, Montenegro, Greece) soon after the declaration and only Vlorë was under the delegates' control. The infobox gives no area for 1912 (the Principality page gives 30,145 km2 for 1916). The 1913 shape takes over in July 1913.

27,676 km2 for 1913-1915 against 30,145 km2 in the Principality infobox for 1916 (ratio 0.92); the League of Nations commission 'reaffirmed Albania's 1913 borders' and the shape is cell-for-cell the 1920 shape. It holds from the Great Powers' decision of 29 July 1913 (Albania page; the Principality page says May 1913); before that, Vlorë only. From late October 1914 Greek forces held the south, and from 1915-1916 foreign armies held most of the country, so the shape is the nominal state, not its control (ledger occupations).

correction.text: Albania within its 1913 borders, as the Principality infobox's 30,145 km2 for 1916 requires; occupied by Italy (Vlorë), Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian forces ('about two-thirds of the country'), Serbia and Montenegro (the north) and Greece ('a sliver')

keyframe_review.note: 5,420 km2 is 0.18 of the infobox's 30,145 km2 for 1916. The gazetteer shows the shape is southern Albania south of 40.5 N (11 of its 18 cells in Gjirokastër county, 5 in Vlorë county, 1 each in Korçë and Berat) - roughly the Northern Epirus that the page has proclaimed in spring 1914 and entered by Greek forces in late October 1914 - not the Albanian state. The page keeps Albania within its 1913 borders throughout the war; drawn here as the 1913 shape with the occupations in the ledger.

correction.text: Albania within its 1913 borders; at 11 November 1918 'Italy's army had occupied most of Albania', Serbia held the northern mountains, Greece 'a sliver' and French forces Korçë and Shkodër

keyframe_review.note: Same 5,323 km2 southern-Albania polygon as 1916 (cell-for-cell), 0.18 of the infobox figure. The Congress of Durrës (December 1918) and the Congress of Lushnjë (27-31 January 1920) restored a government; the 1913 shape is the right outline for 1919.

27,793 km2 for 1920-1935, cell-for-cell the 1913 shape; 28,748 km2 is the modern figure on the Albania page (ratio 0.97). Dated by the Congress of Lushnjë (27-31 January 1920), Italy's withdrawal after the Battle of Vlora (September 1920) and admission to the League of Nations on 17 December 1920; the League commission 'reaffirmed Albania's 1913 borders'. Republic (31 January 1925) and Kingdom (1 September 1928) change the regime, not the outline.
27,820 km2 for 1936-1938, one gazetteer cell (about 250 km2) larger than 1920; no page opened gives a border change, so the 1913 borders stand (Albania page: 28,748 km2 today, ratio 0.97).

correction.text: Albania within its 1913 borders after 'on 7 April 1939 Italian troops' invaded; on 12 April the parliament 'voted to unite the country with Italy' in personal union under Victor Emmanuel III; Zog fled on 9 April

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Albanian shape for 1939-1943 (the Italian rows may contain Albania; for the eu-13 and render agents to reconcile). Outline unchanged; the status is an Italian occupation / protectorate, recorded as occupation_start/_end here and as a vassal tie in Italy's dossier.

correction.text: the 1913 borders plus Kosovo: 'Kosovo and other Albanian-populated territories were united with Albania proper after the conquest of Yugoslavia and Greece by the Axis powers in the spring 1941'; Mussolini 'boasted in May 1941' that he had achieved 'Greater Albania'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 'Greater Albania'. The page names only Kosovo; the other territories (western Macedonia, Plav-Gusinje, Chameria) are not listed or given an area, so only Kosovo (about 10,100 km2 in the gazetteer) is drawn; a gap-filler should open the Greater Albania page. Under German occupation from autumn 1943 the extent is not given.

correction.text: Albania within its 1913 borders (Kosovo no longer included), under German occupation until 'The partisans entirely liberated Albania from German occupation on 29 November 1944' (Tirana on 17 November)

keyframe_review.note: 27,579 km2, 0.96 of the modern 28,748 km2. Outline right; the status is occupied until the end of November, recorded in the ledger. The return of Kosovo to Yugoslavia in 1944 is not on the page.

27,793 km2. A provisional government was 'formed at Berat in October' 1944 with Enver Hoxha as prime minister; the 'Democratic Government of Albania' is the infobox's name. The shape is the 1913 outline again (equal to 1920 cell-for-cell).

region.text: Vlorë, the only town under the delegates' control

ledger.note: 28 November 1912: the Assembly of Vlorë declares Albania independent. 'The Assembly of 40 delegates meeting in southern Albania in the city of Vlorë on 28 November 1912, declared Albania an independent country'; a provisional government under Ismail Qemali followed on 4 December 1912, and 'Vlora was the only town in the whole country under the delegates' control'.

region.text: the lands of the 1913 Albanian borders beyond Vlorë

ledger.note: July 1913: the Great Powers recognise Albania within borders they draw, the Balkan League armies having occupied the land. 'On 29 July 1913 the international community agreed to recognise Albania as a neutral, sovereign and hereditary principality' (the Albania page: 'the Treaty of London delineated the borders of the country and its neighbors'; the Principality page: 'Treaty of London in May 1913'). The lands are the Cliopatria 1913 shape beyond the Vlorë core; the pages name none.

21 February 1914: Albania becomes a principality. Principality infobox 'Established: 21 February 1914' (the Provisional Government dissolved on 22 January 1914 and handed over to the International Control Commission); Prince Wilhelm of Wied arrived at Durrës on 7 March 1914. Same state, same colour.

October 1914: Greek forces enter southern Albania. 'In late October 1914, Greek forces entered Albania' under the Protocol of Corfu's recognized Autonomous Republic of Northern Epirus, which ethnic Greeks had proclaimed in spring 1914 and the Albanian government had recognised; Wilhelm had left on 3 September. The land is the Gjirokastër district, my reading of Northern Epirus; the page gives none.

1916 (page silent on the date): Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian forces occupy about two-thirds of Albania. 'Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian forces then occupied about two-thirds of the country', after a Central Powers offensive scattered the Serbian army; Italy occupied Vlorë and Serbia and Montenegro the north. The page dates none of it; the year is the infobox's area year and Cliopatria's Austria-Hungary neighbour year. Bulgarian forces are not in Cliopatria's Bulgarian shape.

September 1918: the Austro-Hungarian forces leave Albania. 'In September 1918, the Entente forces broke through the Central Powers' lines north of Thessaloniki, and within days Austro-Hungarian forces began to withdraw from Albania.' The end of the withdrawal is undated.

11 November 1918: Italy holds most of Albania. 'When the war ended on November 11, 1918, Italy's army had occupied most of Albania'; it had occupied Vlorë earlier (undated on the page), under the secret Treaty of London of April 1915 promising Italy Vlorë and a protectorate. Italian forces controlled Albanian political activity in the areas they held.
November 1918: French forces hold Korçë and Shkodër. 'French forces occupied Korçë and Shkodër as well as other regions'. The page gives the situation at the armistice, not the day of arrival.

November 1918: Serbia holds the northern mountains. 'Serbia held much of the country's northern mountains'; Serbian troops 'conducted actions in Albanian-populated border areas' in 1919 while Kosovo remained part of Serbia. The district names are my reading of 'the northern mountains'.

1920 (page silent on the date): Greek forces leave the south. The page has Greece occupying 'a sliver of land within Albania's 1913 borders' at the armistice and gives no withdrawal; the year is Cliopatria's restoration of the full 1913 shape in 1920 and the League commission 'reaffirmed Albania's 1913 borders'.
1920 (page silent on the date): French forces leave Korçë and Shkodër. The page lists them at the armistice and does not date their departure; the year is Cliopatria's 1920 shape.
1920 (page silent on the date): Serbian troops leave the northern mountains. The page has them there in November 1918 and acting in the border areas in 1919; the year is Cliopatria's 1920 shape.

January 1920: the Congress of Lushnjë makes Tirana the capital. The congress, held in five sessions on 27-31 January 1920, 'established the High Council ... and moved the capital from Lushnjë to Tirana' (infobox: Durrës 1914-20, Lushnjë 1920, Tirana 1920-24).

region.text: all of Albania except Sazan Island

ledger.note: September 1920: Italy leaves Albania except Sazan. 'In September 1920, after the Battle of Vlora, where Italian-occupied Vlorë was besieged by Albanian forces, Rome abandoned its claims on Albania under the Treaty of London and withdrew its forces from all of Albania except Sazan Island at the mouth of Vlorë Bay.' Admission to the League of Nations followed on 17 December 1920.

31 January 1925: the principality becomes a republic. Infobox '1st Republic of Albania: 31 January 1925'; Zogu's Yugoslav-backed army had retaken Tirana by Christmas Eve 1924 and 'In 1925, the monarchy was abolished' (Principality page, 'Disestablished: 31 January 1925'). Same state, same colour.
1 September 1928: Zog makes Albania a kingdom. Infobox 'Kingdom of Albania: 1 September 1928'; 'In 1928, Zog transitioned Albania from a republic to a monarchy'. Same state, same colour.

7 April 1939: Italy invades Albania. 'on 7 April 1939 Italian troops' invaded; Zog fled to Greece on 9 April and on 12 April 'the Albanian parliament voted to unite the country with Italy', offering the crown to Victor Emmanuel III 'in personal union'. The occupier's dossier should record the protectorate tie.

Spring 1941: Kosovo joins Albania under Italian auspices. 'Kosovo and other Albanian-populated territories were united with Albania proper after the conquest of Yugoslavia and Greece by the Axis powers in the spring 1941'; Mussolini 'boasted in May 1941' of 'Greater Albania'. The page names only Kosovo.
September 1943: Italy capitulates and its occupation of Albania ends. 'When Italy capitulated in September 1943'; the personal union with Victor Emmanuel III ends with it.

Autumn 1943: Germany occupies Albania. 'In the autumn of 1943, Nazi Germany occupied all of Albania after Italy was defeated'; a neutral government of the Balli Kombëtar was formed in Tirana after a deal with the Germans (the infobox: 'Albania (German Client)'). The month is the capitulation's; the page says autumn.
1944 (page silent): Kosovo goes back to Yugoslavia. Cliopatria's 1944 shape is Albania within its 1913 borders; the page does not say when or how Kosovo was separated.

29 November 1944: the partisans free all Albania. 'Tirana was liberated by the partisans on 17 November 1944 after a 20-day battle' and 'The partisans entirely liberated Albania from German occupation on 29 November 1944'; a provisional government had been formed at Berat in October with Enver Hoxha as prime minister.

10 January 1946: the People's Republic replaces the Democratic Government. The Albania page infobox lists '2nd Republic of Albania: 10 January 1946' (the body gives no date) under Enver Hoxha; borders as in 1913. Cliopatria starts its People's Socialist Republic row in 1946.

wars.name: First Balkan War (Albanian lands)

zones.text: the lands of the 1913 Albanian borders, occupied by the Balkan League states

wars.outcome: Albania declared independence on 28 November 1912 during the war; its lands 'were occupied by the Balkan League member states' (Serbia, Montenegro, Greece) until the Great Powers recognised an Albanian principality on 29 July 1913.
wars.note: Albania was not a combatant; the page gives no dates or lands for the occupations. The war page itself was not opened (page budget).

wars.name: Albania in World War I

zones.text: Albania within its 1913 borders, occupied by several armies

wars.outcome: Albania collapses after Prince Wilhelm leaves on 3 September 1914; by 11 November 1918 Italy held most of the country, Serbia the north, Greece a sliver and France Korçë and Shkodër; the Congress of Lushnjë (January 1920) and the Albanian rising force Italy out by September 1920, and a League of Nations commission reaffirmed the 1913 borders.
wars.note: Secret Treaty of London (April 1915) promised Italy Vlorë and a protectorate, Serbia and Montenegro the north and Greece the south.

wars.name: Battle of Vlora
wars.outcome: Albanian forces besiege Italian-occupied Vlorë; in September 1920 Rome abandons its claims and withdraws from all Albania except Sazan Island.
wars.note: The battle page was not opened (page budget).

wars.name: Italian invasion of Albania
wars.outcome: Italian troops land on 7 April 1939; Zog flees on 9 April; on 12 April the parliament votes the union with Italy in personal union under Victor Emmanuel III.
wars.note: General Alfredo Guzzoni led the invasion.

wars.name: German occupation of Albania and the partisan war
wars.outcome: Germany occupies all of Albania in autumn 1943; the partisans liberate Tirana on 17 November 1944 and all Albania on 29 November 1944.
wars.note: The Balli Kombëtar (formed October 1942) formed a neutral government in Tirana after a deal with the Germans.

certainty.note: Only Vlorë was held; the borders were drawn by the Great Powers in July 1913 and not surveyed on these pages.
The 1913 borders are nominal; occupation lines of Italy, France, Serbia, Greece and the Central Powers are approximate.
The 1913 borders reaffirmed by a League of Nations commission.
Italian and German occupation; the Greater Albania lands (Kosovo) are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria rows. 'Albania' 1912-1945 (Q222) is one continuous state through the Provisional Government (1912-1914), the Principality (21 February 1914), the Republic (31 January 1925), the Kingdom (1 September 1928), the Italian personal union (1939-1943), the German occupation (1943-1944) and the Democratic Government; regime changes are rename events. 'People's Socialist Republic of Albania' 1946-1990 (Q467864) is a separate Cliopatria row; the dossier ends on 10 January 1946 (Albania page infobox), so it overlaps that row in 1946 only. 'Republic of Albania' 1991-2024 shares Q467864 with the People's Socialist Republic. Wrong Cliopatria shapes: 1916 and 1919 (5,420 and 5,323 km2, southern Albania below 40.5 N only, 0.18 of the Principality infobox's 30,145 km2 for 1916) are marked wrong and replaced by the 1913 shape with the occupations in the ledger. The 1912 shape (17,682 km2) is the Vlorë assembly's claim; only Vlorë was held. Cliopatria has no Albanian shape for 1939-1943: two new keyframes (Italian union; Greater Albania with Kosovo); the Italian and Axis rows of other groups may also contain Albania in those years, for the render agent to reconcile. Disagreements: the Treaty of London is 30 May 1913 for the Balkan Wars page and 'May 1913' for the Principality page, 29 July 1913 for the Albania and Declaration pages (the Declaration page itself gives 17 May and 29 July); the ledger uses July for the borders. The Principality infobox lists 'Wilhelm I 1914-1925' although he left on 3 September 1914. The Albania page infobox puts the Principality at 29 July 1913; the Principality page at 21 February 1914. Unverified or thin (5-page budget, two pages were thin): the extent of the Greater Albania of 1941-1943 beyond Kosovo (western Macedonia, Plav-Gusinje, Chameria are on no page opened); the date of Kosovo's separation in 1944; the dates of the withdrawals of Greek, French and Serbian forces in 1920 (confidence 1); the Italian occupation of Vlorë and the Austro-Hungarian and Bulgarian occupation (both undated on the page; the year 1916 is Cliopatria's); the Bulgarian occupation named on the Principality page is not in Cliopatria's Bulgarian shapes or in the Bulgarian dossier. Pages that did not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Albanian_Kingdom_(1939%E2%80%931943), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italian_protectorate_of_Albania_(1939%E2%80%931943) and the unencoded variant (url_not_found); 'Italian protectorate of Albania' is a disambiguation page. Counterparts: Northern Epirus (autonomous republic, spring 1914) and the Balkan League occupations are not separate rows; Greece (first-hellenic-republic), serbia (the Cliopatria 1918 row), yugoslavia and yugoslav-partisans are used as slugs from the seed. Native name 'Shqipëria' is not on the pages opened.
